originalTitle: Amy Hunt claims third European Championships gold in relay triumph for ‘fantastic four’
summary: Great Britain’s teams triumphed in both the men’s and women’s 4x100 relays at the European Championships
content: No sooner had Amy Hunt won a staggering third European gold medal in five days than she pointed at the superwomen guiding her closer to history. “We’re the fantastic four,” she said. It was hard to argue with that, especially after watching Britain’s 4x100m women power to glory in 42.05secs, more than 10 metres clear of Switzerland and Poland. “It’s such a privilege to be able to step on the track with these ladies, and the individual superpowers that we bring,” said Hunt. “It’s no joke. We’re all superwomen together out there.” First she addressed Dina Asher-Smith, who ran the first leg and whose gold equalled the Polish sprinter Irena Szewinska’s overall record tally of 10 medals at the championships. “I’m stood next to Dina, she’s the most decorated European athlete in history,” she said. “She has got thousands of medals.” Then Hunt turned to the emerging 21-year-old star Success Eduan, who is three weeks from completing a degree in midwifery. “This girl, Success, is a midwife,” said Hunt. “She brings new babies into the world.” Finally, Hunt pointed to Imani-Lara Lansiquot, who had brilliantly carried the baton home. In 2021 she had also written a play, Armour of Gaza, about growing up in Peckham. “Imani, that girl wrote a play,” said Hunt, clearly deeply impressed. The overall message was clear. On Sunday, Hunt will attempt to become the first athlete to win four gold medals at a single edition of a European championships in the mixed 4x100m relay. But she wanted this night to be about her teammates most of all. And that included praise for Britain’s new relay coach, Richard Kilty, who told the women a simple message before they stepped out on to the track: “Go out and break their hearts.” The British team certainly did that. Everyone played their parts, including the newcomer Eduan, who is now intending to become a full-time sprinter. “I finish in three weeks and I graduate in November, hopefully,” she said. Is it harder to deliver a baby or a baton, she was asked. “A baby! Someone’s life is in my hands,” she said smiling. It was a great night overall for Britain’s relay teams given that 15 minutes earlier the men’s quartet of Jeremiah Azu, Louie Hinchliffe, Zharnel Hughes and Romell Glave also took gold, in 38.45secs, ahead of Germany and Belgium. Before the drama of the relays there were a series of extraordinary performances across the night. The best of them? That surely came in the triple jump, where Italy’s Andy Díaz’s stunning leap of 18.15m – the fourth furthest in history – brought him gold by 39cm from Portugal’s Pedro Pichardo. But not far behind was Sweden’s Andreas Almgren’s destructive display in the men’s 10,000m. After a dawdling first kilometre, Almgren gradually broke the resistance of all his rivals and lapped most of the field, to win by nearly 20 seconds in a championship record 27mins 23.44secs. “If someone is going to beat me, they are going to have to suffer for it,” said Almgren. “I’m in the best 10k shape of my life.” The Swiss athlete Dominic Lobalu took silver, while the world champion Jimmy Gressier won bronze in a sprint finish from Italy’s Yeman Crippa. Soon afterwards, Germany’s Julian Weber broke Steve Backley’s javelin championship record with a monster 90.40m final round throw to beat his compatriot Nick Thumm. “I’m delighted for him,” said Backley. “Julian Weber is my favourite thrower. A brilliant athlete. He has thrown ridiculously far tonight. Records are there to be broken and it is why we love Championships. Medals are for keeps, records are to borrow.” In the women’s 400m, Norway’s Henriette Jaeger was just as impressive as she took gold in 49.04, a second clear of Natalia Bukowiecka of Poland with Lieke Klaver of the Netherlands winning bronze. It was also a great night for Ireland as Kate O’Connor took gold in the women’s heptathlon with a score of 6751. Behind her were two Dutch athletes, Emma Oosterwegel and Sofie Dokter, who scored 6712 and 6664 points respectively. Afterwards, O’Connor dedicated her gold medal to her father and coach, Michael. “He still turns up to training, day in, day out, because this is my dream – but it is also his dream too,” she said. However, Katarina Johnson-Thompson vowed to fight on despite finishing 23rd. “I’ve had a really difficult season behind the scenes, and I didn’t know what form I was going to come here in,” she said. She is reported to have been battling a calf injury. “I obviously trusted myself to perform in major championships. I just didn’t have the preparation that I truly needed to be competitive.” The biggest surprise of the night, meanwhile, came in the men’s 1500m. Most had expected the world champion and silver medallist from 2025, Isaac Nader and Jake Wightman, to be battling it out for gold. But Nader faded to tenth, and Wightman found nothing when leading with 100m to go. And that left Stefan Nillessen, a 6ft 4in 23-year-old, to weave his way through for a shock success in 3:35.70. “The smile won’t go off my face for a long time,” said Nillesen, who runs a bit like Forrest Gump. Finally, in the women’s high jump, Yaroslava Mahuchikh cleared 1.97m to take gold from Poland’s Maria Zodzik and Montenegro’s Marija Vukovic.
chineseTitle: 艾米·亨特在“神奇四侠”接力赛中夺得第三枚欧洲锦标赛金牌
chineseSummary: 英国队在欧洲锦标赛男子和女子 4x100 米接力赛中双双夺冠
chineseContent: 艾米·亨特在五天内赢得了令人震惊的第三枚欧洲金牌后，她就指出了那些引导她更接近历史的女超人。 “我们是神奇的四人组，”她说。很难反驳这一点，尤其是在观看了英国女子 4x100 米以 42.05 秒的成绩夺冠之后，领先瑞士和波兰 10 多米。亨特说：“能够与这些女士以及我们带来的个人超能力一起走上赛道，真是一种荣幸。” “这不是开玩笑。我们都是女超人。”首先，她向迪娜·阿舍-史密斯致辞，她参加了第一回合比赛，她的金牌追平了波兰短跑运动员伊雷娜·斯泽文斯卡 (Irena Szewinska) 在锦标赛上获得 10 枚奖牌的总纪录。 “我站在迪娜旁边，她是历史上获得最多荣誉的欧洲运动员，”她说。 “她获得了数千枚奖牌。”然后亨特找到了 21 岁的新星成功·埃杜安 (Success Eduan)，他距离获得助产士学位还有三周时间。 “这个女孩，成功，是一名助产士，”亨特说。 “她把新婴儿带到了这个世界。”最后，亨特指向伊玛尼-拉拉·兰西科特，她出色地接过了接力棒。 2021 年，她还写了一部关于佩卡姆成长经历的戏剧《加沙之甲》。 “伊玛尼，那个女孩写了一部戏剧，”亨特说道，显然印象深刻。总体信息很明确。周日，亨特将力争成为第一位在欧洲锦标赛 4x100 米混合接力赛上夺得四枚金牌的运动员。但她希望今晚最重要的是她的队友们。其中包括对英国新任接力教练理查德·基尔蒂的赞扬，他在女子走上赛道之前告诉她们一个简单的信息：“出去吧，伤透她们的心。”英国队确实做到了。每个人都扮演了自己的角色，包括
